tips: Version Q executes a textbook open-format BPM jump across a 2:3 tempo ratio. Instead of letting the outgoing 87 BPM tempo or key clash with the incoming 130 BPM house groove, it captures the final vocal snippet into a high-passed, syncopated eighth-note delay freeze that acts as a rhythmic house riser, landing with high impact right on the downbeat.
A subtle white-noise riser sweep or a slight high-pass filter roll-off on the outgoing master during the last half-bar before 0:24 would make the drop into Song B hit even harder.

P and Q both execute the transition intelligently by dropping Song B's house beat right when Song A's original drums cut out at the bridge, allowing the vocal phrase ('big lights will inspire you') to conclude cleanly at 23s without trainwrecking. R ruins the blend by letting the next vocal phrase start and chopping it off mid-word.

Apply a high-pass filter or low EQ cut to Song A right as Song B's kick drops at 20s to eliminate the subtle low-mid clash from the piano, and add a light dub echo/reverb tail to the final vocal word ('you') to melt it cleanly into the incoming house groove.

Version R lets the full two-bar vocal phrase play out ('These streets will make you feel brand new, big lights will inspire you') and applies a clean echo tail that resolves right on the house drop at 0:23, avoiding both Q's awkward empty hole and P's jarring truncated vocal.
Add a subtle white noise riser, sweep, or short snare roll under the final vocal tail to build even more anticipation into the 130 BPM drop.
Version Q executes a clean, deliberate drop on the 1 right as the vocal hook resolves, avoiding both the dead-air drag of P and the sloppy chopped vocal collision of R.
Add a subtle dub echo or wash of reverb on 'inspire you' to bridge the acoustic ballad space into the punchy house intro seamlessly.
